basis: Defining cystic dysplasia affects kidneys and pancreas; bowed lower limbs are part of the syndrome. Situs reversal alone does not establish cardiovascular damage.
Melanoma arising in the ciliary body of the eye.
Progressive CNS neurodegeneration with neuronal loss, parkinsonism and supranuclear gaze palsy; ocular motor symptoms do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Complement-mediated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury; thrombotic microvascular injury is defining, with hypertension in 30-79%.
Inherited keratinization disorder of oral mucosa; the definition supports gastrointestinal involvement rather than cutaneous disease.
Organic acid metabolism disorder; developmental impairment and seizures affect most patients, and cardiomyopathy occurs in approximately half of type 2 cases.
Inherited calcium-sensing disorder with hypercalcemia; renal impairment and stones occur in 5-29%. Common structural bone damage is not established.
Inherited hair-shaft disorder causing brittle, sparse hair and alopecia, sometimes with follicular keratosis or nail abnormalities.
Usually infectious inflammation of sphenoid sinus mucosa; paranasal sinuses belong to the airway axis, and the bone itself is not the defined site.
Giant bullous emphysema causes irreversible destruction of pulmonary parenchyma.
Defining bent-bone dysplasia; intellectual disability is frequent (30-79%). Dental, thyroid and blood abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
Coronary arterial smooth-muscle spasm narrows the lumen and reduces myocardial blood flow.
Inherited organic acid metabolism disorder without a consistent damaging phenotype; developmental and white-matter abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Inherited epilepsy with intellectual disability in 16/25; nystagmus in 6/15 does not establish intrinsic eye damage. Facial dysmorphism adds no damaged organ.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; intellectual disability affects 18/19. Ocular abnormalities are individually below 30%.
Parasitic lymphatic infection; chronic skin thickening and hyperkeratosis occur in 30-79%. Renal and pulmonary abnormalities are below 30%; eyelid disease is not typical.
Ulceration directly damages the esophageal wall.
Congenital joint contractures and mandibular hypoplasia define skeletal involvement; webbed neck and hypoplastic nipples do not establish another organ disorder.
Mitochondrial complex I deficiency with lactic acidosis; severe neonatal encephalopathy is typical (>30%). Hypotonia and hypoventilation alone add no muscle or lung damage.
Malignant rhabdoid tumor arising in soft tissues; the supplied definition identifies a soft-tissue sarcoma rather than a renal or CNS primary.
Carcinoma arising from the ovary as a reproductive organ; endocrine dysfunction is not defining, and advanced stage does not establish a common specific organ metastasis.
Astrocytoma occupying the pineal body, a CNS structure and endocrine gland; both anatomical axes apply to the defined tumor location.
Primary congenital glaucoma, with or without anterior segment dysgenesis, directly affects the eye.
Etiologic umbrella spanning many organ systems, with no shared organ axis across most diseases; inheritance alone does not imply a metabolic disorder.
Malignant tumor of the third cranial nerve; impaired eye movements from nerve dysfunction do not establish intrinsic ocular disease.
